source_text: PRAEFATIO Prima praefatio nostra uiam erranti demonstrat Respectumque bonum, cum uenerit saeculi meta, Aeternum fieri, quod discredunt inscia corda. Ego similiter erraui tempore multo Fana prosequendo parentibus insciis ipsis; Abstulit me tandem inde legendo de lege, Testifico Dominum: doleo pro ciuica turba, Inscia quod pergit periens deos quaerere uanos; Ob ea perdoctus ignaros instruo uerum. 1 INDIGNATIO
pass_a_gloss: Preface: show way to wanderer; eternal stake; author once erred; Law rescued; now instructs.
pass_b_english: Our first preface shows the way to the one who wanders, and the good regard that comes when the world’s turning-point arrives — to become eternal, which ignorant hearts refuse to believe.

I myself wandered a long time the same way, chasing shrines, my parents not knowing better. Reading the Law finally pulled me out. I testify to the Lord: I grieve for the civic crowd that goes on perishing, seeking empty gods. So, taught at last, I instruct the ignorant in the truth.

choices.english: the way to the one who wanders
choices.why: Commodian’s catechetical frame; not Didache’s exact “two ways” wording in this preface.

anf_compare.notes: Prior English used Didache-style “two ways” slogan; locked preface is conversion/way-for-wanderer instruction, not a duplicate Didache 1.
